business_problem: Novo Nordisk needed to shorten the slow and error-prone process for producing clinical study reports while keeping document generation deterministic and regulator-friendly in a tightly controlled pharmaceutical environment.
solution_summary: Novo Nordisk built NovoScribe on MongoDB Atlas to support structured authoring for clinical study reports. Atlas stores approved text snippets, vectors, and case-specific trial data such as tables, lists, statistical outputs, and analytical results. The application uses a prompt-search-retrieval loop built around large language models and retrieval-augmented generation: Atlas retrieves relevant approved passages, the system presents five candidate text options to a human reviewer, and the chosen language is written back to the database before the next document section is assembled. That pattern keeps a human in the loop while still automating repetitive authoring work in a regulated setting where deterministic output matters. By combining reusable content modules with study-specific data inside Atlas, NovoScribe can build long CSR drafts section by section in minutes instead of weeks while reducing manual rework and keeping scientific staff focused on higher-value review work.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores approved text, vectors, and study data and supports the retrieval workflow that assembles clinical study reports.

data_flow: Approved text snippets and trial data are stored in MongoDB Atlas, the application retrieves relevant context for each prompt, a human reviewer selects from five candidate passages, and NovoScribe assembles report sections into a complete clinical study report.
business_outcome: MongoDB helped Novo Nordisk cut report-writing times by 90%, reduce staffing required for CSR creation, and produce regulator-friendly drafts far faster while keeping humans in control.
